FE-018.title: Financial Engine V4
FE-018.description: The project's settled commercial calculation system that produces Commercial Performance results from warehouse facts and published business rules.
FE-018.formula: Sales = Σ priceWithDisc; Marketplace Fees = explicit Finance fee/service suffixes; Sales-to-Settlement Difference = Sales − forPay; Revenue = Σ ppvz_for_pay; Estimated Tax = Tax% × Σ finishedPrice; Net Profit = Revenue − costs − Estimated Tax

FE-016.title: Model B (Commercial Performance)
FE-016.description: The primary commercial profitability model for historical reporting: money-flow from sales through expenses to Net Profit on the Dashboard and related reports.

FE-017.title: Model C (Settlement Profit)
FE-017.description: Settlement-oriented profit framing (historically Model C). Revenue = netForPay; Net Profit deducts logistics, storage, penalties, deductions, acceptance, product cost, and advertising. Marketplace fees are informational only.
FE-017.formula: Revenue = netForPay; Net Profit = netForPay − Logistics − Storage − Penalties − Deductions − Acceptance − Product Cost − Advertising
exceptions: Marketplace Fees are informational only and must not be deducted in Model C.

FE-001.title: Gross Sales
FE-001.description: Gross merchandise sales for completed sales in the period, before subtracting returned sales in the Commercial Performance display story.
FE-001.formula: Gross Sales = Σ priceWithDisc (completed sales, pre-return display)

FE-002.title: Net Sales
FE-002.description: Display sales after returns: Gross Sales minus Returned Sales. Used for seller-facing sales presentation; not a synonym for Revenue.
FE-002.formula: Net Sales = Gross Sales − Returned Sales; Sales = Σ priceWithDisc

FE-003.title: Revenue
FE-003.description: In Commercial Performance, the seller's marketplace payable amount for the period — the commercial top line from which operating costs and Estimated Tax are reasoned toward profit.

FE-004.title: Marketplace Fees
FE-004.description: The marketplace fee take in the commercial fee story. Shown for understanding; not deducted again in Net Profit when already reflected before Revenue.
FE-004.formula: Marketplace Fees = abs(commission) + abs(acquiring_fee) + abs(ppvz_reward) + abs(ppvz_vw) + abs(vw_nds)
exceptions: Never includes generic OTHER, logistics, storage, acceptance, penalties, adjustments, advertising, or compensation.
Not the same as Sales-to-Settlement Difference or signed WB Remuneration.

FE-005.title: Product Cost
FE-005.description: Cost of goods attributed to sold units for the period, based on maintained unit costs.

FE-006.title: Logistics
FE-006.description: Marketplace logistics costs attributed to the selected period in Commercial Performance.

FE-007.title: Storage
FE-007.description: Marketplace storage costs for the period.

FE-008.title: Acceptance
FE-008.description: Marketplace acceptance (intake) operation costs for the period.

FE-009.title: Penalties
FE-009.description: Marketplace penalty amounts for the period.

FE-010.title: Adjustments
FE-010.description: Marketplace financial adjustments for the period, including advertising and other holds not classified as Fee, Logistics, Storage, Acceptance, or Penalties.

FE-011.title: Advertising
FE-011.description: Advertising/marketing spend. In Commercial Performance commonly included inside Adjustments when sourced from finance adjustments.

FE-012.title: Estimated Tax
FE-012.description: Historical reporting tax estimate on completed sales. In Commercial Performance: Tax Rate × Σ finishedPrice (Customer Paid). Smart Pricing uses a different base intentionally.
FE-012.formula: Estimated Tax = Tax Rate × Σ finishedPrice (historical reporting / Financial Engine)
exceptions: Smart Pricing uses Tax Rate × (Sale Price − legacy Sales-to-Settlement allowance) — do not unify with reporting.

FE-013.title: Net Profit
FE-013.description: Commercial profit after Estimated Tax in Commercial Performance — the primary after-tax profitability KPI for historical reporting.
FE-013.formula: Net Profit = Revenue − Product Cost − Logistics − Storage − Acceptance − Penalties − Other/Adjustments − Advertising − Estimated Tax

FE-014.title: WB Settlement
FE-014.description: Settlement-oriented view of marketplace payout figures for reconciliation. Distinct from Commercial Performance; not a replacement commercial P&L.
exceptions: Revenue (Commercial Performance) ≠ Settlement Amount / Seller Payout.

FE-015.title: Return Handling
FE-015.description: Returns affect the sales story (Gross Sales, Returned Sales, Net Sales) and related quantities. They do not redefine Revenue into Customer Paid or Net Sales.

FE-019.title: priceWithDisc
FE-019.description: Wildberries Sales API seller-discounted unit price. Basis for Sales = Σ priceWithDisc on completed sales. Stored as wb_sales.price_with_disc. Not finishedPrice or forPay.

FE-020.title: finishedPrice
FE-020.description: Sales API customer-paid amount (finishedPrice). Persisted as wb_sales.revenue. Basis for historical Estimated Tax = Tax% × Σ finishedPrice. Not Commercial Performance Revenue.
FE-020.formula: Estimated Tax = Tax Rate × Σ finishedPrice

FE-021.title: forPay
FE-021.description: Sales API seller-payable per sale (forPay). With Net Sales it derives the Sales-to-Settlement Difference. Stored as wb_sales.for_pay. Differs from Finance ppvz_for_pay.

FE-022.title: ppvz_for_pay
FE-022.description: Finance API payable field per transaction. Commercial Performance Revenue = Σ ppvz_for_pay. Stored in wb_finance. Can differ from Sales API forPay.

FE-023.title: netForPay
FE-023.description: Settlement-oriented net payable used in Model C where Revenue = netForPay. Distinct from Commercial Performance Revenue.

FE-024.title: Acquiring Fee
FE-024.description: Payment acquiring costs (Finance ACQUIRING). Component of marketplace cost presentation.

FE-025.title: PPVZ VW
FE-025.description: Finance PPVZ_VW fee component in marketplace cost presentation.

FE-026.title: PPVZ Reward
FE-026.description: Finance PPVZ_REWARD component in marketplace cost presentation.

FE-027.title: Sales vs Revenue Distinction
FE-027.description: Sales (Σ priceWithDisc) is merchandise presentation. Revenue (Σ ppvz_for_pay) is seller payable. Not interchangeable.

FE-028.title: Units Sold
FE-028.description: Completed non-return sale units in period from wb_sales (is_return = false).

FE-029.title: Returned Units and Net Units
FE-029.description: Returned Units from is_return sales. Net Units = Units Sold minus returns. Distinct from Returned Sales value.

FE-030.title: Orders KPI
FE-030.description: Order events from wb_orders by order_date. Distinct from Units Sold (completed buyouts).

FE-031.title: Buyout
FE-031.description: Demand-to-sale conversion between orders and completed sales. Chart 'Purchases' label = Buyout, not Purchases module.

FE-032.title: Profit Margin
FE-032.description: Ratio from Commercial Performance (Net Profit vs Revenue/Sales per surface). Presentation only.

FE-033.title: Return Logistics
FE-033.description: RETURN_LOGISTICS finance category — return shipment costs. Distinct from Returned Sales and forward Logistics.

FE-034.title: Sale Date vs Finance Settlement Date
FE-034.description: Sales metrics: sale_date. Finance/Revenue/costs: operation_date. Orders: order_date. Settlement: finance/settlement time. Do not merge date axes.

FE-035.title: Sales API vs Finance API Reconciliation
FE-035.description: Sales forPay and Finance ppvz_for_pay differ by feed/timing/settlement. Revenue uses Finance. Sales-to-Settlement Difference uses Sales − forPay. State API and date axis when reconciling.

FE-036.title: Effective Marketplace Cost Presentation
FE-036.description: Canonical Marketplace Fees: explicit commission + acquiring_fee + ppvz_reward + ppvz_vw + vw_nds suffixes from wb_finance. Generic OTHER is excluded.

BIZ-001.title: Accounting Rules Framework
BIZ-001.description: Canonical accounting framework for money-related calculations and reports. Defines financial models, revenue recognition boundaries, and cost categories.

ARCH-001.title: Estimated Tax Dual Model
ARCH-001.description: The project intentionally maintains two Estimated Tax bases: historical reporting uses Σ finishedPrice; Smart Pricing uses Sale minus its legacy Sales-to-Settlement allowance. Do not unify.

relationships.note: Defines tax dual-model policy for FE-012

exceptions: Reporting: Tax Rate × Σ finishedPrice
Smart Pricing: Tax Rate × (Sale − legacy Sales-to-Settlement allowance)

DASH-001.title: Dashboard Commercial Performance
DASH-001.description: Primary seller dashboard presenting Commercial Performance KPIs (Revenue, Net Profit, costs, settlement, operational metrics) for a scoped Company/Marketplace Account and inclusive date range. Reads warehouse facts via Financial Engine V4 — does not call live marketplace APIs.

aliases: Which date does the Dashboard use

DASH-002.title: Dashboard Date Range
DASH-002.description: Dashboard uses URL query params from/to (YYYY-MM-DD) via resolveScopedDateRange. Default: last 30 calendar days inclusive. Presets: 7, 30, 90, 180 days. Sales KPIs filter wb_sales.sale_date; Finance KPIs filter wb_finance.operation_date; Orders filter wb_orders.order_date — all inclusive [from, to].

DASH-003.title: Dashboard Account and Scope Selection
DASH-003.description: Dashboard KPIs are scoped by Company and Marketplace Account (and optional brand/product filters via URL scope params). Multi-tenant isolation: figures always relative to selected marketplace_account_id.

DASH-004.title: Dashboard Revenue Card
DASH-004.description: Shows Commercial Performance Revenue = Σ Finance ppvz_for_pay for completed sales in scope (Financial Engine V4). Date axis: wb_finance.operation_date aligned with sales period. Not Gross Sales, Net Sales, or Settlement Amount.
keywords: what does the dashboard revenue card show

DASH-005.title: Dashboard Gross Sales Card
DASH-005.description: Shows Gross Sales — Σ priceWithDisc on completed sales before return subtraction in display story. Date axis: wb_sales.sale_date. Distinct from Revenue card.

DASH-006.title: Dashboard Net Profit Card
DASH-006.description: Shows Commercial Performance Net Profit = Revenue − costs − Estimated Tax (Model B / FE V4). Primary after-tax profitability KPI. Does not use Settlement Profit unless user switches to Model C view.
DASH-006.formula: Net Profit = Revenue − Product Cost − Logistics − Storage − Acceptance − Penalties − Other − Advertising − Estimated Tax

DASH-007.title: Dashboard Marketplace Fees Card
DASH-007.description: Shows canonical Finance-based Marketplace Fees from explicit commission, acquiring_fee, ppvz_reward, ppvz_vw, and vw_nds suffixes. The breakdown separately exposes signed WB Remuneration and Sales-to-Settlement Difference.

DASH-008.title: Dashboard Settlement Card
DASH-008.description: Presents WB Settlement / settlement-oriented figures for reconciliation — distinct from Commercial Performance Revenue and Net Profit. Uses settlement framing (Model C / wb-settlement). Not interchangeable with Revenue card.

DASH-009.title: Dashboard Operational KPIs
DASH-009.description: Operational metrics: Units Sold, Returned Units, Net Units from wb_sales; Orders/Cancelled/Active from wb_orders (order_date); Buyout/conversion between orders and sales. Purchases chart label = Buyout (Glossary), not Purchases module.

DASH-010.description: Dashboard Revenue card = Commercial Performance Σ ppvz_for_pay. Settlement card = payout/settlement framing. Difference is intentional — Revenue answers commercial payable; Settlement answers cash transfer reconciliation.

SP-001.title: Smart Pricing Purpose
SP-001.description: Forward-looking pricing decision support: simulates unit economics and solves sale price for target margin. Separate financial model from Commercial Performance (Accounting Rules §3.3). Does NOT modify Financial Engine, Dashboard, Purchases, or Cost Management.

relationships.note: References FE concepts; does not own them

SP-002.title: Adaptive Logistics
SP-002.description: Resolves per-unit logistics from historical data with hierarchy: PRODUCT_HISTORY when completed units ≥ 20, else CATEGORY_HISTORY when category units ≥ 50, else ACCOUNT_HISTORY fallback. Thresholds: SMART_PRICING_MIN_PRODUCT_LOGISTICS_SALES=20, SMART_PRICING_MIN_CATEGORY_LOGISTICS_SALES=50.
keywords: when does product history apply logistics

relationships.note: SP uses historical logistics; FE uses period logistics

SP-003.title: Legacy Sales-to-Settlement Pricing Proxy
SP-003.description: Smart Pricing currently uses the weighted historical Sales-to-Settlement Difference from Sales API: difference = Sales − forPay, percent = difference/Sales. It is explicitly isolated from canonical Finance-based Marketplace Fees until the denominator and no-double-count backtest are approved.

relationships.note: Finance presentation differs from SP historical %

exceptions: Finance COMMISSION rows not used for SP fee rate

SP-004.title: Profit Simulator
SP-004.description: Client-side simulation (/analytics/simulator, Smart Pricing UI) solving price for target profit under stated assumptions. Does not persist changes to product costs, Financial Engine, Dashboard, or warehouse data. Simulated ≠ actual profitability.
keywords: does profit simulator change real product costs

SP-005.title: Smart Pricing Date Range
SP-005.description: Smart Pricing historical inputs default to a 30-day lookback window for product/category/account history resolution unless overridden. Uses sale_date scoped sales and matching finance rows for adaptive costs.
keywords: what is the default date range

SP-006.title: Historical Cost Resolution Hierarchy
SP-006.description: Unified adaptive resolution for fees, logistics, storage: PRODUCT_HISTORY when product completed units ≥ 20; CATEGORY_HISTORY when category units ≥ 50; ACCOUNT_HISTORY fallback. Insufficient history → fall back to next tier or account/default commission.

SP-007.description: Smart Pricing does NOT modify Financial Engine, Dashboard calculations, or historical Commercial Performance. Uses a different Estimated Tax base after its legacy Sales-to-Settlement allowance per ARCH-001. References fee concepts but solves forward prices — not period P&L.

SP-008.title: Smart Pricing Estimated Tax
SP-008.description: Smart Pricing Estimated Tax = Tax Rate × (Sale Price − legacy Sales-to-Settlement allowance). Intentionally different from Financial Engine historical tax (Tax% × Σ finishedPrice). Do not unify.

ADM-001.title: Administration Purpose
ADM-001.description: Operational control plane for Companies, Marketplace Connections, users/roles, security, audit, and platform settings. Governs tenancy and access — does NOT own Financial Engine calculations, Reporting math, Smart Pricing, or Warehouse sync engines.

ADM-002.title: Administration Shell
ADM-002.description: Administration UI shell at /administration with navigation to Companies, Connections, Users, Roles, Security, Audit, Warehouse ops, Platform Settings, System Health. Presentation layer only.

ADM-003.title: Company Workspace
ADM-003.description: Administration Companies area owns Company records, currency, tax rate inputs (stewarded business settings), and company-scoped configuration. Distinct from Platform Settings (global presentation).

relationships.note: Tax rate stewarded at company level

ADM-004.title: Marketplace Connections
ADM-004.description: Administration Connections owns marketplace account credentials and connection settings enabling Sync. Credentials stored server-side — never exposed to client. Administration owns credential stewardship; sync engines consume credentials.

ADM-005.title: Users and Roles
ADM-005.description: Administration Users and Roles manage identities, memberships, marketplace access grants, and role-based permissions. Authorization decisions use RLS + server-side checks.

ADM-006.title: Security and Audit
ADM-006.description: Security administration: authentication integration, authorization policies, audit logs with audit reason and correlation ID, security event visibility. Does not expose credentials, ciphertext, tokens, or encryption keys in UI or knowledge.

ADM-007.title: Platform Settings
ADM-007.description: Platform-wide settings via platform-config provider: platform name, default language/timezone, date/number formats, localization, theme, notifications, feature flags, data retention knobs. Stored through administration-platform-settings-service — single SoT for platform prefs.
exceptions: Company currency/tax → Company Workspace, not platform settings

ADM-008.description: Administration OWNS: companies, connections/credentials, users, roles, security, audit, platform settings, warehouse operational UI. Does NOT OWN: Financial Engine, Reporting calculations, Smart Pricing, Product Analytics math, warehouse sync engines, or Net Profit computation.

ADM-009.description: Authentication: verify user identity (login/session). Authorization: enforce permissions via roles, RLS, and server-side requireAuth checks. Administration configures both; business modules enforce authorization on every API route.

ADM-010.title: Administration Secret Handling
ADM-010.description: Marketplace API keys and secrets are server-side only (encrypted storage). Orion knowledge and Administration UI must never expose credentials, ciphertext, tokens, or encryption keys.

ADM-011.title: Feature Flags
ADM-011.description: Feature flags stored in platform settings document, read via platform-config isFeatureEnabled(). Administration Settings UI toggles flags — business modules query provider, not UI.

ADM-012.title: Data Retention Settings
ADM-012.description: Platform data retention preferences (e.g. warehouseHistoryDays for inventory snapshot retention default 90 days) configured in Platform Settings, consumed via getDataRetentionPreferences(). Administration sets policy; warehouse services enforce.

ADM-013.title: Theme and Localization
ADM-013.description: Presentation preferences: theme (light/dark), default language, timezone, date/number formats via platform localization settings. ThemeProvider applies theme client-side from platform config.

ADM-014.title: Warehouse Administration UI
ADM-014.description: Administration warehouse routes provide operational visibility (health, sessions, queue, checkpoints, scheduler) — read-only over warehouse operations. Does NOT own or execute sync engines.

WH-001.title: Warehouse Platform Overview
WH-001.description: The Warehouse Platform persists marketplace operational facts (orders, sales, finance, stock, daily inventory snapshots) for reporting and analytics. Business modules such as Financial Engine and Dashboard read warehouse tables — they do not call live marketplace APIs for historical reporting. Warehouse owns data ingestion, continuity, checkpoints, sessions, and operational visibility — not commercial KPI formulas.

WH-002.title: Warehouse Platform Ownership Boundaries
WH-002.description: Warehouse Platform owns: marketplace fact persistence, sync/backfill orchestration, inventory snapshot continuity, checkpoints, sync sessions, operation history, and the Warehouse Control Center operational UI. Warehouse does NOT own: Financial Engine formulas (Revenue, Net Profit, Estimated Tax), Smart Pricing, Dashboard commercial KPI calculations, or marketplace credential administration. Operational control (sync health, sessions, queue) is separate from business reporting (Commercial Performance, Warehouse Sales Analytics UI).

WH-003.title: Warehouse Data Architecture
WH-003.description: Core warehouse datasets: wb_orders (commercial order events), wb_sales (completed sale/return events), wb_stock (current stock observations), historical_inventory_snapshots (daily historical inventory), warehouse_sync_sessions (Sprint 10 sync runs), warehouse_checkpoints (incremental cursors), warehouse_operation_history (audit trail). Commercial transactions: wb_orders, wb_sales, wb_finance. Current stock: wb_stock. Historical inventory: historical_inventory_snapshots. Operational state: sessions, checkpoints, entity sync state.

WH-004.title: wb_orders Dataset Role
WH-004.description: wb_orders stores marketplace order events scoped by marketplace_account_id. Used by Warehouse Sales Analytics for Orders count and Orders Amount (order demand). Filtered by order_date within the selected inclusive date range. Warehouse column groups rows; NULL warehouse aggregates to Unknown Warehouse. Written primarily by legacy Dashboard Sync (WbSyncService.syncOrders); Sprint 10 incremental sync also upserts orders. Not used for inventory snapshots or Financial Engine Revenue.

WH-005.title: wb_sales Dataset Role
WH-005.description: wb_sales stores marketplace sale and return events. Warehouse Sales Analytics uses completed sales only (is_return = false) for Units and Revenue, filtered by sale_date within the inclusive date range. Revenue = Σ(price_with_disc × quantity) — this is Warehouse Sales Analytics revenue, NOT Financial Engine Revenue (ppvz_for_pay). Warehouse column groups rows; NULL → Unknown Warehouse. inventory snapshots are NOT a source for warehouse sales.

relationships.note: FE Revenue uses ppvz_for_pay — different basis

WH-006.title: wb_stock Dataset Role
WH-006.description: wb_stock holds current marketplace stock observations (warehouse × SKU grain). Represents point-in-time current inventory, not historical inventory. Used for Current Inventory UI and Warehouse Location discovery. Historical stock at a past date requires historical_inventory_snapshots or Inventory History — not wb_stock alone. Legacy Dashboard Sync writes wb_stock via syncStock when the marketplace API succeeds.

WH-007.title: historical_inventory_snapshots Dataset Role
WH-007.description: historical_inventory_snapshots stores daily historical inventory at grain: marketplace_account_id + snapshot_date + warehouse + nm_id + size (+ seller_article, barcode). Source for Inventory History and past-date stock questions (e.g. stock 15 days ago). NOT used by Warehouse Sales Analytics. Populated by daily capture (WB Analytics wb-warehouses API) and CSV archive import — not by legacy order/sales sync.
keywords: which data source contains historical stock

WH-008.title: Warehouse Sync Sessions
WH-008.description: Warehouse Sync Sessions record Sprint 10 Warehouse Platform sync runs (historical backfill and incremental sync engines). Each session tracks entity, status, timing, and progress. Created by warehouse backfill/incremental engines — NOT by legacy Dashboard Sync (WbSyncService). Visible in Warehouse Control Center → Sessions. Dashboard Sync does not create warehouse sync sessions.

relationships.note: Legacy sync does not create sessions

WH-009.title: Warehouse Checkpoint
WH-009.description: A Warehouse Checkpoint stores the incremental sync cursor for a marketplace account and entity (last processed window/date). Incremental sync depends on checkpoints to resume without reprocessing full history. Checkpoints are managed by Sprint 10 warehouse engines and visible in Warehouse Control Center. Legacy Dashboard Sync does not use warehouse checkpoints.

WH-010.title: Warehouse Operation History
WH-010.description: Warehouse operation history records auditable warehouse platform actions (sync triggers, continuity ticks, admin operations). Provides traceability for operational debugging alongside sync sessions and checkpoints. Read by administration and Warehouse Control Center diagnostics — not used for business KPI calculations.

WH-011.title: Warehouse Sales Analytics
WH-011.description: Warehouse Sales Analytics reports order demand and completed sales performance grouped by warehouse location for a selected date range. Data sources: wb_orders (Orders, Orders Amount by order_date) and wb_sales completed rows (Units, Revenue by sale_date). Does NOT use historical_inventory_snapshots or wb_stock. UI: /inventory/warehouse-sales. NULL warehouse → Unknown Warehouse. Returns excluded from Units/Revenue (is_return = false).
keywords: what does warehouse sales analytics use

aliases: Warehouse revenue vs Financial Engine revenue
WH-012.title: Warehouse Sales Analytics Revenue Basis
WH-012.description: Warehouse Sales Analytics Revenue = Σ(price_with_disc × quantity) on completed wb_sales rows. This is intentionally different from Financial Engine Revenue (Σ ppvz_for_pay on completed sales). Do not conflate Warehouse Sales Analytics revenue with Commercial Performance Revenue. Both are verified; they answer different questions.
WH-012.formula: Revenue = Σ(price_with_disc × quantity) on completed wb_sales
exceptions: Financial Engine Revenue uses ppvz_for_pay — see FE-003

WH-013.title: Warehouse Location Model
WH-013.description: A Warehouse Location is a stable internal reporting/grouping concept for a shipping location (WB FBO warehouse or FBS seller location). Implemented as exact trimmed warehouse name string — aggregation key and filter key. displayName comes from presentation aliases. type (wb | fbs) is metadata only — never drives KPI or accounting branches. Active flag indicates observation in stock/orders/sales.

WH-014.title: FBS Warehouse Locations
WH-014.description: FBS is NOT a separate Warehouse module. FBS shipping locations are Warehouse Locations with type metadata fbs (vs wb). Multiple FBS locations are supported when observed in data (e.g. FBS Moscow, FBS Kazan, МП Коломна, МП Электросталь per warehouse-name-aliases). FBS locations participate in the same Warehouse Sales Analytics and location catalog as WB warehouses. Type must not introduce separate business calculation branches.

WH-015.title: Warehouse Location Identity
WH-015.description: Current implementation: Identity = exact trimmed raw marketplace warehouse name string (observation → identity). Canonical display name = formatWarehouseName() via warehouse-name-aliases (presentation only — does not change grouping key). Aliases map multiple raw strings to one display label but grouping remains exact name match. type = wb|fbs from name regex. External WB warehouse ID enrichment is NOT implemented — no separate location ID table exists. If marketplace renames a warehouse string, it appears as a new location until manually aliased for display.
keywords: what happens if warehouse name changes
exceptions: Separate internal location UUID table is planned/future — not implemented

WH-016.title: Warehouse Location Discovery
WH-016.description: Warehouse locations are discovered automatically by unioning distinct non-null warehouse values from wb_stock, wb_sales, and wb_orders for the account. buildWarehouseLocations dedupes by exact trimmed name. Unknown/raw marketplace strings appear as locations when first observed — no pre-registration required. Display aliases (warehouse-name-aliases.ts) affect labels only, not discovery or grouping. historical_inventory_snapshots is not a discovery source in current implementation.

WH-017.title: Warehouse Reporting Date Ranges
WH-017.description: Warehouse Sales Analytics uses URL query params from and to (YYYY-MM-DD) via resolveScopedDateRange. Default when omitted: last 30 calendar days inclusive of today (buildInclusiveDateRange(30)). DASH-004@1.0.0.title: Dashboard Revenue Card

DASH-008@1.0.0.title: Dashboard Settlement Card

SP-001@1.0.0.title: Smart Pricing Purpose
SP-001@1.0.0.description: Forward-looking pricing decision support: simulates unit economics and solves sale price for target margin. Separate financial model from Commercial Performance (Accounting Rules §3.3). Does NOT modify Financial Engine, Dashboard, Purchases, or Cost Management.

relationships.note: References FE concepts; does not own them

SP-002@1.0.0.title: Adaptive Logistics

SP-004@1.0.0.title: Profit Simulator
